exhibition_i18n.heading: This exhibition revisits one of the most ambitious projects of the late Ottoman Empire. By 1908 the Hijaz Railway connected Damascus to Medina, modernising the Hajj for pilgrims while providing political, strategic, and economic advantages to the empire across diverse territories. The significance of the railway and its effects on culture and trade are revealed in photographs, objects, documents, and personal accounts. Though the railway's operation fell victim to the conflicts of World War I, its influence continues to resonate through the region.
